source.section: IT 1040 lines 1 to 8a (bundle PDF p.1); booklet PDF p.16 lines 1 to 4; PDF p.17 line 4 exemption table and line 8a; PDF p.18 bracket table; PDF p.5 rounding; MAGI PDF p.8; MAGI less exemptions worksheet PDF p.40; Schedule of Adjustments line 13 (PDF p.20); business income PDF p.11

worked: Federal AGI = self-employment person 0 60,000.00 = 60,000.00. Federal taxable income = 60,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 44,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored; Ohio starts from federal AGI). IT 1040 line 1 federal AGI 60,000.00. Schedule of Adjustments additions: line 1 non-Ohio state or local interest 0.00; line 12 total 0.00; line 2a 0.00. Deductions: none; line 47 total 0.00; line 2b 0.00. Line 3 Ohio AGI = 60,000.00 + 0.00 - 0.00 = 60,000.00. Line 4: MAGI is line 3 with no business income deduction, 60,000.00, in the band 40,001 to 80,000: 2,150.00 each; 1 exemption x 2,150.00 = 2,150.00. Line 5 = 60,000.00 - 2,150.00 = 57,850.00. Line 6 taxable business income 0.00. Line 7 = 57,850.00. Line 8a tax: 57,850.00 is in the 26,050 to 100,000 band: 342.00 plus 2.750% of (57,850.00 - 26,050.00 = 31,800.00) = 342.00 + 874.50 = 1,216.50. Schedule of Credits line 1 = 1,216.50. MAGI less exemptions (worksheet PDF p.40) = 60,000.00 - 2,150.00 = 57,850.00 (equal to line 7 without business income), under 100,000.00. Line 2 retirement income credit: no covered retirement income, 0.00. Line 4 senior citizen credit: no one is 65 or older, 0.00. Line 10 credits = 0.00 + 0.00 = 0.00. Line 11 = 1,216.50 - 0.00 = 1,216.50. State income tax 1,216.50. The form works in whole dollars ('Round all figures to the nearest dollar', PDF p.5): line 8a would be 1,217; expected keeps the formula result. The form deducts the first 250,000 of business income on line 13 (PDF pp.11, 20): line 3 is 0.00, MAGI 60,000.00 after the add-back, line 5 and line 7 0.00, tax 0.00. Expected follows the projection, which leaves self-employment income in the brackets. Federal AGI here ignores the deduction for half of self-employment tax.
accepted_approximations: Self-employment income is taxed in the brackets, and MAGI is taken as Ohio AGI and MAGI less exemptions as Ohio taxable income (exact without business income). Ohio deducts the first 250,000 of business income, taxes the rest at 3%, and adds the deduction back in MAGI.
